title: Neurocutaneous syndromes and phakomatoses

steps.tx: **Neurofibromatosis type 1** is an autosomal dominant neurocutaneous disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in the NF**1** gene encoding **neurofibromin** on chromosome **17**q11.2, leading to hyperactivation of the cellular Ras-MAPK oncogenic signaling pathway throughout neural crest derivatives and surrounding connective tissues.
steps.say: Neurofibromatosis type 1 is an autosomal dominant neurocutaneous disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in the NF1 gene encoding neurofibromin on chromosome 17q11.2 leading to hyperactivation of the cellular Ras-MAPK oncogenic signaling pathway throughout neural crest derivatives and surrounding connective tissues.

left.title: Genetic & Molecular Basis
points: Mutations in the NF1 tumor suppressor gene
Loss of function causes unchecked Ras hyperactivation

right.title: Clinical Spectrum
points: Optic pathway gliomas and iris Lisch nodules
Risk of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors

steps.tx: Diagnostic criteria for neurofibromatosis type 1 require two or more cardinal features including: **6** or more **café-au-lait** macules greater than **5** mm in prepubertal or **15** mm in postpubertal individuals, axillary or inguinal freckling known as **Crowe sign**, **2** or more neurofibromas or one plexiform neurofibroma, optic glioma, and **2** or more iris Lisch nodules.
steps.say: Diagnostic criteria for neurofibromatosis type 1 require two or more cardinal features including: 6 or more café-au-lait macules greater than 5 mm in prepubertal or 15 mm in postpubertal individuals axillary or inguinal freckling known as Crowe sign 2 or more neurofibromas or one plexiform neurofibroma optic glioma and 2 or more iris Lisch nodules.

rows: 6 or more (>5 mm prepubertal, >15 mm postpubertal)
Clusters of small pigmented macules in skinfolds
2 or more cutaneous or 1 plexiform neurofibroma
Focal soft cutaneous nodule or diffuse nerve mass
Plexiform carrying risk of malignant change
2 or more Lisch nodules or optic pathway glioma
Iris hamartomas on slit-lamp or visual deficit
Pilocytic astrocytoma of anterior visual path

steps.tx: Neurofibromatosis type **2** is caused by mutations in the NF2 gene on chromosome **22**q12.2 encoding merlin or **schwannomin**, defined by pathognomonic bilateral **vestibular schwannomas**, multiple meningiomas, and spinal ependymomas. Patients typically present in early adulthood with progressive sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, and balance impairment.
steps.say: Neurofibromatosis type 2 is caused by mutations in the NF2 gene on chromosome 22q12.2 encoding merlin or schwannomin defined by pathognomonic bilateral vestibular schwannomas multiple meningiomas and spinal ependymomas. Patients typically present in early adulthood with progressive sensorineural hearing loss tinnitus and balance impairment.

right.title: Merlin Tumor Suppressor
points: Encoded by NF2 gene on chromosome 22q12.2
Regulates contact inhibition and Hippo signaling
Absence of café-au-lait preponderance or Lisch nodules

steps.tx: **Tuberous sclerosis** complex is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations in TSC**1** encoding **hamartin** on chromosome **9**q34 or TSC**2** encoding tuberin on chromosome **16**p13.3, triggering constitutive hyperactivation of the downstream mechanistic target of rapamycin signalling pathway and multiple organ hamartomas.
steps.say: Tuberous sclerosis complex is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations in TSC1 encoding hamartin on chromosome 9q34 or TSC2 encoding tuberin on chromosome 16p13.3 triggering constitutive hyperactivation of the downstream mechanistic target of rapamycin signalling pathway and multiple organ hamartomas.

vis.alt: Diagram illustrating cortical tubers, subependymal nodules, and cutaneous features in tuberous sclerosis.
vis.caption: Tuberous sclerosis complex hamartomatous lesions and mTOR activation (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Patients with tuberous sclerosis present with facial **angiofibromas**, ash-leaf hypomelanotic macules, shagreen patches, subependymal giant cell **astrocytomas**, cardiac rhabdomyomas, and bilateral renal angiomyolipomas. Cortical tubers and subependymal nodules frequently cause intractable infantile spasms and pharmacoresistant focal epilepsy in affected children.
steps.say: Patients with tuberous sclerosis present with facial angiofibromas ash-leaf hypomelanotic macules shagreen patches subependymal giant cell astrocytomas cardiac rhabdomyomas and bilateral renal angiomyolipomas. Cortical tubers and subependymal nodules frequently cause intractable infantile spasms and pharmacoresistant focal epilepsy in affected children.

rows: Giant cell astrocytomas near foramen of Monro
Triad of blood vessels, smooth muscle, and fat

steps.tx: Targeted mTOR inhibitors including **everolimus** and sirolimus serve as approved medical therapy to regress subependymal giant cell astrocytomas and bilateral renal **angiomyolipomas** in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex. Pharmacological inhibition of mTORC1 suppresses tumour cellular proliferation, decreases vascularity, and stabilizes long-term renal and cerebral lesions.
steps.say: Targeted mTOR inhibitors including everolimus and sirolimus serve as approved medical therapy to regress subependymal giant cell astrocytomas and bilateral renal angiomyolipomas in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex. Pharmacological inhibition of mTORC1 suppresses tumour cellular proliferation decreases vascularity and stabilizes long-term renal and cerebral lesions.

left.title: Mechanism of mTOR Inhibition
points: Constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivity from TSC loss
Halts unchecked protein synthesis and cell growth

right.title: Clinical Indications in TSC
points: Renal angiomyolipomas >3 cm at risk of rupture

steps.tx: **Sturge-Weber** syndrome is a non-inherited congenital neurocutaneous disorder caused by somatic mosaic mutations in GNAQ, presenting with a facial port-wine stain in the V**1** trigeminal distribution, ipsilateral leptomeningeal angiomatosis, and distinctive gyriform **tram-track** cortical calcifications on neuroimaging. Patients present with early focal seizures, contralateral hemiparesis, and congenital glaucoma.
steps.say: Sturge-Weber syndrome is a non-inherited congenital neurocutaneous disorder caused by somatic mosaic mutations in GNAQ presenting with a facial port-wine stain in the V1 trigeminal distribution ipsilateral leptomeningeal angiomatosis and distinctive gyriform tram-track cortical calcifications on neuroimaging. Patients present with early focal seizures contralateral hemiparesis and congenital glaucoma.

left.title: Clinical Triad
points: Facial port-wine stain (naevus flammeus in V1)
Refractory focal seizures and contralateral hemiparesis
Congenital choroidal angioma and early glaucoma

right.title: Pathological Neuroimaging
points: Gyriform tram-track cortical calcifications on CT

steps.tx: **Von Hippel-Lindau** disease is an autosomal dominant condition linked to mutations in the VHL tumor suppressor gene on chromosome **3**p25, predisposing to retinal and cerebellar capillary **hemangioblastomas**, clear cell renal cell carcinomas, and adrenal pheochromocytomas. Impaired degradation of hypoxia-inducible factor drives excessive vascular endothelial growth factor secretion and hypervascular tumorigenesis.

Impaired degradation of hypoxia-inducible factor drives excessive vascular endothelial growth factor secretion and hypervascular tumorigenesis.
